newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokuyo City sees some 67 bln yen in problem loans.
newsitem.headline: Tokuyo City sees some 67 bln yen in problem loans.

text.p: Tokuyo City Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it estimated its problem loans would be about 67 billion yen at the end of March against an actual 70.30 billion yen at the end of last September.
The second-tier regional bank based in Sendai, northern Japan, said in a statement it would need to dispose of about 40 billion yen out of the estimated problem loans in future.

It estimated its problem loans at the end of March would include about 11 billion yen in bad loans to bankrupt firms and about 44 billion yen in non-performing loans, on which interest payments were in arrears by six months or more.
They would also include about 12 billion yen in restructuring loans on which customers were allowed to cut or waive interest payments in view of restructuring efforts.
Tokuyo City worked out a five-year restructuring programme in March last year in which it aims to cut problem loans to a manageable level, it said.
Through the restructuring programme, including a cutback in personnel costs, the bank estimates its operating profit will rise to 5.0 billion yen in 2000/2001.
In 1996/97, it sees operating profit at 2.8 billion yen, down from actual 4.9 billion yen in 1995/96, it said.
The bank said that while there may be concerns that it could have more problem loans than publicly announced, it has revealed the amount of such loans under clear definitions.
The amount of loans whose repayment was in question was much smaller than the amount of problem loans, it said.
